note:
TECHNIQUE / MEASURED -- A STANDING DRAINER SURVIVES THE SESSION THAT STARTED IT, IS INVISIBLE TO EVERY QUEUE INSTRUMENT, AND THE NEXT OPERATOR WILL START A SECOND ONE. I did exactly that tonight. The flock held, nothing was corrupted, and the near-miss is worth more than the outcome.

WHAT I FOUND, AFTER I HAD ALREADY RACED IT. A previous session left a loop at

  /tmp/claude-1000/-home-nathan-Projects-hornvale/f1a159e3-.../scratchpad/dr

whose own header reads, in capitals, ONE LOOP ONLY. A second waiter races this one for the same queue. It drains stage and census automatically and deliberately leaves merge to a human vet. It is a good design. I could not see it.

WHY I COULD NOT SEE IT. Three separate instruments say nothing about it:

  make sluice-status        shows ROWS, never the loops that consume them
  census-run.sh status      shows the CLAIM HOLDER, one process, not waiters
  the queue row note        says "launched by the drain loop" -- which loop is
                            not a field, because there was only ever one

I read all three before acting and none of them could have told me. The only instrument that shows it is ps, and you have to already suspect.

AND IT IS ORPHANED, WHICH IS THE PART THAT GENERALISES. Its parent is pid 1:

  684536       1 bash /tmp/claude-1000/.../f1a159e3-.../scratchpad/dr

The session that started it is gone; systemd reparented the loop and it kept draining. So "the previous operator's session ended" does not mean their automation ended. A scratchpad path is session-scoped; the PROCESS started from it is not.

THE COLLISION, TIMED TO THE SECOND. Both waiters were chained to the same event -- the in-flight census drain exiting -- so they fired together:

  13:42:37Z  their drain claims campaign/the-tidemark (stage), takes the flock
  13:42:38Z  my   drain claims the astronomy census delivery (merge), blocks

Measured state one minute later:

  pid 3076761  sluice-run.sh req-1a21e863d825  HOLDS  /tmp/hv-census.lock
  pid 3077231  sluice-run.sh req-799ad4e2a7f4  child: flock -w 7200 9
  census-run.sh status: heavy running, sluice-stage:campaign/the-tidemark

One holder, one waiter, and the waiter's ONLY child is the flock. No row ran twice: sluice-queue.sh claim is atomic under its own lock, so two simultaneous claims get two DIFFERENT rows rather than one row twice.

WHY NO WORKTREE CORRUPTION, CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. scripts/sluice-run.sh takes the flock at line 707 and does not touch the shared chamber worktree until line 788, where the checkout --force and reset --hard live. Every mutating operation is inside the lock. Had the ordering been the other way the two jobs would have reset the same tree under each other, and both would have reported on a tree neither built. The ordering is load-bearing and it is not obvious from reading either script alone.

THE ACTUAL LESSON, WHICH IS NOT ABOUT LOCKS. Decision 0133 says the claim absorbs contention, and it did -- that part of the design is vindicated under a real unplanned double-drain, which is better evidence than the eight-waiter trial that ratified it. What the claim cannot absorb is POLICY: their loop refuses to auto-drain merges on purpose, and mine drained three. That divergence is invisible to the mutex, because a mutex orders work and has no opinion about which work should exist. Two correct loops with different policies produce an incoherent queue, serially and with a green light the whole way.

WHAT I WOULD WANT INSTEAD, and I am not building it unasked. The queue has no way to say "a drainer is attached, this is its policy". A pidfile under $HV_SLUICE_DIR written by whatever drains, checked by whatever is about to start draining, and surfaced in make sluice-status, would have refused me in milliseconds and cost nothing -- the same shape as the claim itself, one level up. Note that their loop ALREADY writes a pidfile, to its own scratchpad, where nobody else can find it.

WHAT I DID. Left both running, because the arrangement is stable by luck and killing a loop mid-job is worse: their max_jobs=1 loop takes only stage and census, there are none queued behind the-tidemark, so it idles at sleep 60 while my drain finishes the three merges I vetted. Both then stop competing. If you are the next operator: run ps -ef | grep sluice-drain BEFORE you start anything, and read the script behind any pid you find, because its policy is not in this repo.
